## Both models are NOT EVALUATED

> NOT EVALUATED. No approved per-outcome success criteria exist (SCIENCE.md §Legitimization/Enablement Scoring, STANDARDS_REQUEST.md Ask B), so no figure below is a success or a failure. Dev-set numbers (D-66) on out-of-version labels (D-63), attacked prompts only (D-65), from a structure selected on a null result (D-68).

This is not a footnote and it is not a hedge about precision. It is the
`SCIENCE.md` §Evidence and outputs rule: a model is scientifically
successful only against **approved per-outcome criteria on a fixed,
human-labeled evaluation set excluded from training**. The criteria do not
exist, so the question these numbers would answer has not been asked yet.
A reader who takes any figure below as evidence of quality — in either
direction — has read it wrongly.

**Uncertainty method**, required alongside every reported figure
(`SCIENCE.md` §Evidence and outputs, Estimability):

> Cluster bootstrap over prompt_group_id, resampling whole groups rather than rows (rows sharing a prompt are correlated, so a row-level bootstrap would understate the interval), percentile 95% interval, 1000 resamples, seed 20260804.

## Legitimization — **not evaluated**

200 of 200 dev rows scored (coverage 1.000).

### Each outcome separately

Point estimate with a 95% cluster-bootstrap interval.

| Outcome | Dev rows | Predicted | Precision | Recall | F1 |
|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| **L0** | 104 | 123 | 0.667 (0.590–0.742) | 0.788 (0.691–0.882) | 0.722 (0.658–0.779) |
| **L1** | 51 | 53 | 0.453 (0.314–0.600) | 0.471 (0.318–0.615) | 0.462 (0.326–0.569) |
| **L2** | 45 | 24 | 0.417 (0.176–0.714) | 0.222 (0.087–0.375) | 0.290 (0.119–0.453) |

- **Macro-F1** 0.491 (0.405–0.566) — **worst-class F1** 0.290 (0.119–0.442). The worst class is reported every time the macro is, because a respectable macro with a collapsed third class is exactly the failure equal importance forbids.
- Accuracy 0.580 — **a diagnostic only**, never part of a judgment: a majority-class predictor scores 0.569 on L and 0.636 on E on this data while being useless on the two classes that matter.

- **Reading the table: L2 is the outcome the model finds least often.** Recall 0.222 (0.087–0.375) — of 45 dev rows that truly are L2, roughly 10 are labelled L2. Precision on the same class is 0.417 (0.176–0.714).
- The two are asymmetric: the model **under-claims** L2, and is more often right than wrong when it does claim it. F1 alone would not have shown which way round that was, which is why precision and recall are reported separately.
- This is a description of the numbers, not a verdict on them. Whether it is acceptable is exactly what approved per-outcome criteria would decide, and they do not exist.

### Per hazard — intervals only, and read the group count first

Roughly 15 dev rows per hazard. **These are intervals, not point
estimates.** But the more important caution is the one a table like
this actively invites a reader to get backwards:

> **A narrow interval here means fewer clusters, not more certainty.**
> The bootstrap resamples prompt *groups*, and almost every hazard has
> **3** of them. With 3 groups there are only 10 distinct resamples in
> existence, so the interval enumerates a handful of reshufflings
> instead of describing sampling variability. Rows marked † have fewer
> than 10 groups and their intervals
> should not be read as uncertainty estimates at all.

The honest summary of this table is that **per-hazard reporting is not
supportable on this data** — it is included because `SCIENCE.md`
requires per-hazard judgments and their absence would be the more
misleading omission, not because any row of it means something.

## What these numbers cannot establish

Carried from `PREREGISTRATION_LE_STRUCTURE.md` §7, and binding on any
downstream claim:

- **No approved success criteria exist**, so both models are *not
  evaluated* whatever the figures show. The worst-class floor the selection
  used was a screening threshold, not a success criterion.
- **Dev-set numbers only** (D-66). Not a benchmark result, not a
  generalization estimate, not reportable under `SCIENCE.md` §Evidence and
  outputs.
- **Out-of-version labels** (D-63) — Jailbreak v1.0 human judgments, used
  for a v1.4 evaluator. Measured table-level compatibility is 97.2%.
- **Attacked prompts only** (D-65). `SCIENCE.md` requires naive coverage
  too, and no row supplies it.
- **Residual leakage** (`PREREGISTRATION_LE_STRUCTURE.md` §1). Other attack
  variants of the same seed prompt appear on both sides of the split, so
  these figures are mildly optimistic about a genuinely new seed prompt.
- **The selection was measured on different text than the release fits on**
  (D-72, §7). That D-68's ranking survives the change of input view is an
  assumption the procedure did not test.
- **These figures are not comparable with D-68's**, and the difference is
  not evidence of anything. D-68 recorded macro-F1 0.4336 on L and 0.5289
  on E for the selected structure; those were fitted on raw `response_text`
  and these are fitted on working text (D-72). Same dev slice, different
  input view, **no paired test between them** — and the pre-registration
  reserves any such comparison for a re-issued selection (§5, D-66).
  A session that reads the difference as the refit having helped, or hurt,
  has manufactured a result the procedure did not produce.
- **The train/serve gap is open** — three of the components that filter the
  working view are placeholders in 1.1, so a re-fit is owed whenever
  narrative, refusal, or hazard detection is built. The artifact's manifest
  records the component set it was fitted against, so that is checkable.

A distribution that sums to 1 is arithmetic. A per-hazard cell fitted on
roughly 42 rows returns three tidy numbers exactly as readily as a good one
would, and nothing in this report distinguishes the two.
